evidence_scale.documented: published by the marketplace (or its official dev docs), or confirmed on a global guide
evidence_scale.reported: third party, owner email, or the pilot document
evidence_scale.assumed: proposed or inferred in our own specs or code
evidence_scale.playbook: Opptra Catalog Playbook (internal, unverified against marketplaces)

conflicts.topic: Title formula: five different orderings
options: C: per-channel formulas (Noon/Namshi, Trendyol, Amazon, Myntra)
conflicts.recommendation: Per-channel check; one internal generation default of Brand + Gender + Product Type + Key Feature/Material, with colour and size left to the variant attributes. Only the presence checks are block (starts with brand, gender, product type); the order is a warn.
conflicts.reasoning: A and B are mutually exclusive on word order and B adds colour/size that the same playbook says should not differentiate titles (L546, L853 'unique per product, not per colour'). Channel formulas (Amazon, Noon) put type near the start. Marketplace search ranks on presence of terms, not order beyond the first ~60 characters, so a presence check loses little and cannot produce false blocks. Needs a channel manager confirmation.

conflicts.topic: Title length: general 60-200, Amazon '1509', Myntra 90 vs 60, Namshi 200 vs 150
options: Amazon: 150 vs 200 (real Amazon limit is category specific, read from product type definition)
conflicts.recommendation: Noon 150, Namshi 200 (hard) with 150 warn, Trendyol 100, Amazon 150 (treat 1509 as a typo of 150, verify with the SP-API product type definition for Amazon.ae and Amazon.in), Myntra block above 90, warn above 60. Make the general 60 minimum a warn that applies only where the channel maximum is 100 or more.
conflicts.reasoning: Both Myntra numbers appear in the playbook; blocking at the lower number would reject titles the quick reference allows, blocking at the higher may let rejected titles through, so surface both until Myntra confirms. 'Write to the shortest limit first' plus a 60 minimum gives exactly one legal length on Myntra, so the minimum cannot be universal.

conflicts.topic: Bullet count: 4-5 vs 5 vs 5-7 vs 'up to 10'
conflicts.recommendation: Generate exactly 5 bullets; check 4-5 as block for all channels except Trendyol (5-7).
conflicts.reasoning: 5 satisfies every cell of both sources, so the conflict disappears at generation time. Check strictness only matters for imported brand copy.

conflicts.topic: Bullet length and style: 80 vs 100 vs 100-250 vs 160; no end punctuation; ALL CAPS
options: Follow the playbook's own examples (about 85 characters, full stops, ALL CAPS label words)
conflicts.recommendation: Per-channel limits (Noon/Namshi <=80, Myntra <=100, Trendyol <=160, Amazon 100-250); no end punctuation as a warn; ALL CAPS first word allowed on Amazon only. Ignore the example bullets as authority.
conflicts.reasoning: No single length satisfies both '<=80' and Amazon '>=100'; the content has to be generated per channel (the formatting stage in Catalog v2 L13 already assumes this). The playbook example bullets violate the 80-character limit and the no-punctuation rule, so they cannot be used as calibration.

conflicts.topic: Description limit: 'under 1,000 for all' vs no limit vs 30,000 vs 2-3 sentences
options: Per channel as in the quick reference
Trendyol dense keyword text up to 30,000
conflicts.recommendation: Master description under 1,000 characters (warn). Channel hard limits: Amazon and Myntra 1,000 (block), Trendyol 30,000 (block), Noon and Namshi none. Treat Trendyol's '2-3 sentences' as a generation hint only.
conflicts.reasoning: Under 1,000 is a safe authoring target that passes everywhere, and per channel limits stop unneeded false blocks. The Amazon number should be re-read from the product type definition (real caps differ from 1,000).

conflicts.topic: Minimum image resolution: 1200x1800 for all vs 1000x1000 vs per-channel minima vs code
conflicts.recommendation: Separate two things: (1) intake quality bar for brand photos = 1200x1800 as a warn; (2) channel output rule = per-channel minima from documented sources (Noon width>=660, Trendyol exactly 1200x1800, others per code). Drop the 1000x1000 takeaway.
conflicts.reasoning: 1000x1000 is a square and contradicts 'min 1200x1800' for portrait fashion; the code already enforces per-channel canvases and the Crops spec says a small source is flagged, not skipped (min 500 px). Intake bar and output bar are different questions.

conflicts.topic: Aspect ratio / canvas: playbook vs code vs published (Noon, Namshi, Trendyol, Amazon, Shein, VogaCloset)
options: Playbook ratios (Noon 1:1 or 4:5, Namshi 4:5, Trendyol 2:3, Amazon 1:1, Myntra 3:4)
conflicts.recommendation: Use numbers, not the labels: Trendyol 1200x1800 (2:3, documented), Amazon any ratio with long side >=1000 and main image white (do not block 1:1 vs 3:4), Noon between 0.5 and 1 with width >=660 (3:4 passes), Namshi follow the playbook 4:5 min 1200x1500 until the Namshi manager confirms (currently code treats it as Noon). Correct the stale sheet texts in channels.ts (Trendyol 3:4, Amazon 3:4, Styli 1200x1600).
conflicts.reasoning: Where the code's behaviour (canvas numbers) and its own label disagree, the canvas is what ships, so the label is the drift. For Noon the only published rule is ratio >=0.5, so playbook 1:1 or 4:5 is stricter than the marketplace. Namshi has no public rules; the stricter documented-by-playbook value avoids a rejection.

conflicts.topic: Maximum file size: playbook 10/8/5/10/1 MB vs code 2 MB
conflicts.recommendation: Keep the 2 MB internal cap (below every limit except Myntra) and add Myntra at 1 MB only when Myntra goes live, after confirming the figure.
conflicts.reasoning: 2 MB satisfies Noon, Namshi, Trendyol (5) and Amazon; Myntra 1 MB for a 1500x2000 image is unusually tight and is likely a mistake (1 MB would force heavy compression).

conflicts.topic: File format: JPEG/PNG vs JPEG only vs JPEG/TIFF
conflicts.recommendation: Output always sRGB JPEG (as code does); accept PNG or TIFF at intake.
conflicts.reasoning: JPEG is accepted by every channel, including the stricter Noon (documented JPEG only), Trendyol and Myntra; PNG 'accepted' on Noon in the playbook contradicts the Noon help page.

conflicts.topic: Background colour: light grey 'RGB 240+' vs code #E0E0E0 vs 'White' vs Amazon white
options: Move to #F0F0F0 or lighter to meet 'RGB 240+'
conflicts.recommendation: Owner decision needed. Default: keep #E0E0E0 only if the original rules-sheet source for it can be shown; otherwise move to >=240 grey for Noon/Namshi/Trendyol/Myntra. Image 1 on Amazon (and Shein) stays #FFFFFF.
conflicts.reasoning: #E0E0E0 = 224 fails the playbook's own '240+' test, and Noon's published rule is 'light grey recommended for fashion' without a value. The code note says it was 'encoded exactly' from a rules sheet we cannot see; the tolerance BG_TOLERANCE 24 would still pass a 240 background, so lightening has no technical cost.

conflicts.topic: Hero image type: lifestyle allowed vs forbidden on Noon, Myntra and Amazon; no flat lay hero
options: Image 1 may be lifestyle (playbook L184, L1730)
Image 1 always a clean packshot/on-model on plain background
conflicts.recommendation: Image 1 = clean on-model (or packshot for non-apparel) on the channel background for every channel; lifestyle only in slots 2+.
conflicts.reasoning: Noon (documented), Myntra (playbook) and Amazon (documented) all forbid lifestyle in the main slot, so the stricter option costs nothing on the others and removes channel-specific hero regeneration. This also matches the 01/02 shot lists, which put FM or FL first.

conflicts.topic: Product fill of frame: 75-85 vs Amazon 85 vs Myntra 80-90 vs code margins
conflicts.recommendation: Channel specific, all warn except geometry margins from code (block): Amazon >=85 (no maximum), Myntra 80-90, others 75-85.
conflicts.reasoning: Amazon states a minimum (about 85 percent) and has no maximum, Myntra is a different band; the code's margins already give a hard, measurable box so fill percentage should only warn.

conflicts.topic: DPI: 72 vs 96 vs 300
options: Per-channel DPI metadata as in code
conflicts.recommendation: Keep per-channel DPI from code (Trendyol 96 documented); treat 300 as a recommendation for infographics (warn).
conflicts.reasoning: DPI is a metadata tag that does not change pixels; the only documented numbers are Noon >=72 and Trendyol 96. Do not block on the 300 figure.

conflicts.topic: On-model requirement by category and channel
options: Playbook: on-model for all adult apparel and a model shot in every QA
Noon published: recommended only; kids flat
conflicts.recommendation: Category scoped: required for adult tops, bottoms, dresses, outerwear, sports; not required for footwear, accessories, lingerie, swimwear, kids, multipack (use the 01 rows). Severity block on Amazon and Namshi/Trendyol/Myntra (playbook), warn on Noon (documented as 'recommended').
conflicts.reasoning: The QA line 'model shot included' contradicts the playbook's own Myntra statement that flat lay is acceptable for accessories and the 01 spec for flat-lay lingerie. Treat the QA line as imprecise.

conflicts.topic: Image count: min 6, Noon 3, Voga 4, Amazon 5-7 vs up to 9, Myntra 1-7, Noon 10, Namshi/Trendyol 8
conflicts.recommendation: Target 6 or more images (warn below 6). Hard maxima: Noon 10, Namshi 8, Trendyol 8, Amazon 9 (7 are shown), Myntra 7. Counting video as slot 8 outside the image count.
conflicts.reasoning: Playbook 'Max 7' on Amazon is the number displayed, not the upload limit; blocking at 7 could hide valid extra images but not cause rejection, so keep it as a warn at 7 and block at 9. The 8-slot sequence includes video, so images stay <= 7.

conflicts.topic: Units: cm vs inches (size chart slide text vs size chart section), and mixed units within innerwear
options: Inches for apparel (L1511, L1578, L1667, L1750)
conflicts.recommendation: Store one canonical unit (cm), render inches for India apparel and cm for GCC channels, and print both on the chart image; keep bra band in cm and foot length in cm. The check is: no mixed units inside one chart.
conflicts.reasoning: Inches is stated four times in the size chart section, cm three times in the shot slides; they cannot both be right for the same apparel image. India sizes are conventionally in inches, GCC in cm; the playbook does not distinguish. A single stored unit with derived display removes the data entry error the playbook warns about (L1693).

conflicts.topic: Footwear size systems required
options: Per channel (Amazon UK+EU+IN, Myntra all four, spec slide EU/UK/US)
conflicts.recommendation: Capture all four systems always; validate the per-channel subset (Amazon UK, EU, IN; Myntra all four). Skip IN for GCC channels.
conflicts.reasoning: 'US required on all platforms' (L1406) contradicts Amazon's own requirement in the same playbook (L1438). Capturing all four costs one conversion table and satisfies every channel.

conflicts.topic: Close-up shot: RECOMMENDED vs mandatory
options: Mandatory for fabric products (DO and QA)
conflicts.recommendation: Mandatory as warn for fabric products; code shot lists already include FC on every channel.
conflicts.reasoning: Two of three statements say mandatory, the 01/02 channel tables all include a fabric close-up. Making it warn avoids blocking non-fabric products (e.g. footwear 'top view').

conflicts.topic: Infographic mandatory (slot 3) vs Noon 'only photographs, no unwanted text' and Amazon main rules
options: Infographic where text overlay is allowed (Amazon secondary, Trendyol), warn elsewhere
conflicts.recommendation: Mandatory on Amazon and Trendyol and Myntra (playbook), warn on Noon and Namshi until the channel manager confirms a text overlay is accepted; never in image 1.
conflicts.reasoning: Noon publishes 'only photographs' and 'no unwanted text'; an overlay infographic is not clearly covered ([NOT FOUND] in research). A block rule could force an infographic that Noon rejects.

conflicts.topic: Two different shot taxonomies: playbook 8 slots vs the 01/02 channel shot lists
options: Playbook: hero, side, infographic, back, full model, close-up, size chart, video
01/02: FM, FL, FC, BH, HS (head and shoulders), per channel
conflicts.recommendation: Keep two layers: Layer A the photographic shot list per channel and garment type (01 section 4.2 plus 02); Layer B the add-on slots (infographic, size chart, video) from the playbook, generated by a separate step and appended after Layer A. Side view and head and shoulders are not interchangeable and should be explicit.
conflicts.reasoning: The two lists were written for different purposes (brand photo QA vs a cropping engine) and neither contains the other: 01/02 have no side view, infographic, size chart or video; the playbook has no head-and-shoulders and no waist-down shots. A merged list invents rules nobody wrote.

conflicts.topic: Keywords: 8-10 vs 250 bytes (Amazon) vs Trendyol none vs mandatory
conflicts.recommendation: Amazon: block above 250 bytes. Noon/Namshi/Myntra: 8-10 phrases as warn. Trendyol: not applicable (do not block an empty field).
conflicts.reasoning: The playbook's own table says Trendyol has no backend keywords, yet the QA lists them as mandatory. The unit is also unclear (the example holds 8 phrases but about 20 words); define as phrases for non-Amazon and bytes for Amazon.

conflicts.topic: Promotional words list includes 'Top', which is also a product type
options: Block promotional phrases only (Top Rated, Top Quality, Best, #1, Sale)
conflicts.recommendation: Block list without bare 'Top': Best, #1, Sale, Guaranteed, Amazing, Cheap, 'Top Rated/Quality/Selling'.
conflicts.reasoning: The playbook's own category example is 'Casual Strappy Tank Top' (L549-550), so the literal word list rejects a compliant title.

conflicts.topic: Special characters @ # & * vs brand names, parentheses, slash and dashes in the playbook's own examples
options: Allow & inside a registered brand name
conflicts.recommendation: Block @ # * and URL characters; allow '&' only inside the exact brand name; allow ( ) / - and the pipe.
conflicts.reasoning: Examples include '(220 GSM)', '/' and dashes; many brands contain '&' (H&M, Marks & Spencer). A pure character block would corrupt the brand name, which the playbook also requires to be exact (L996).

conflicts.topic: Active tops and bottoms shot tables are copied from the bottoms and footwear slides
options: Use Tops (for sports tops) and Bottoms (for sports bottoms) rules
conflicts.recommendation: Reuse the tops and bottoms rules; sports bras use the innerwear size chart (bra band + cup).
conflicts.reasoning: The Activewear (Top) slide text talks about rise height, leg cut, back pockets and 'critical for denim'; the reference labels say 'Half Model / On-Foot', copied from footwear. Matches 01 section 4.2 ('sports tops' share the tops row, 'sports bottoms' share the bottoms row).

conflicts.topic: Footwear attribute slide has duplicate and mislabelled rows
options: Encode from the Footwear Specifications slide only
conflicts.recommendation: Encode from L991-1052 (the clean attribute slide) only; treat L1416-1460 duplicates (Sole Material twice, 'Warranty' holding gender values, 'Country of Origin' holding Adult/Teen/Kids) as copy errors; accept Almond (toe) and Leather (sole) as additions.
conflicts.reasoning: The size chart slide repeats 'Sole Material' for the ankle/shaft values, 'Warranty' for the gender values, and 'Country of Origin' for the age group; the clean slide has all of these correctly labelled.

conflicts.topic: Allowed value lists drift between the attribute slides and the size-chart slides
options: Per-channel taxonomy mapping (Amazon PTD, Trendyol API, Noon NIS)
conflicts.recommendation: Union as the internal canonical vocabulary, mapped per channel from the channel's own lists (the research notes none are public for Noon, Namshi); Fade as the enumerated Fade Type.
conflicts.reasoning: Neither list is authoritative: tops fit has 4 vs 5 values, neck 4 vs 6, pattern 4 vs 5, bottoms fit 4 vs 6 values, Fade is Yes/No vs a five-value enum. Marketplaces validate against their own lists, so the internal vocabulary only needs to be a superset that maps cleanly.

conflicts.topic: HSN codes look wrong or incomplete
options: Encode the playbook lists as validation
Format-only check plus a finance-owned lookup table
conflicts.recommendation: Format-only check now (numeric, 4 to 8 digits, chapter 61/62 for apparel, 64 for footwear). Do not enforce the playbook's HSN lists until finance or the customs broker supplies a table.
conflicts.reasoning: My reading of the HS chapters, to be verified: 6211 covers track suits, swimwear and other woven garments, not shorts (shorts are 6103/6104 knitted or 6203/6204 woven); 6212 is bras, girdles and corsets, so the playbook puts bras under the wrong code and swimwear under it; 6109 (knitted T-shirts, the playbook's own example) is missing from the tops list; the ranges on L1775 (6105-6114, 6203-6211) disagree with the lists on L1525 and L1590. Enforcing wrong codes would create tax errors.

conflicts.topic: SLA promise vs platform review time
options: 48/72 hours to ready-for-upload plus +48 hours platform review
conflicts.recommendation: Define the SLA clock as 'submitted to the marketplace' and show platform review separately.
conflicts.reasoning: L147 says 48 hours from submission to live, while L1379-1381 adds 48 hours for Amazon and Myntra review, so the live promise is unreachable on those channels. L147 also limits 72 hours to footwear/accessories 'with infographics' while L1367-1371 does not.

conflicts.topic: Bottoms attribute list omits Brand and MRP/HSN; innerwear etc. require them
options: Add Brand, MRP and HSN to bottoms
conflicts.recommendation: Add them (block) because the Content QA lists MRP and HSN for all listings and Title QA needs the brand.
conflicts.reasoning: Clear omission: the bottoms slide has 15 rows where tops has 16 and brand/MRP/HSN are the three that differ.

conflicts.topic: Code vs research: VogaCloset, Shein, Namshi and Styli canvases are assumed, research shows different numbers
options: Keep code canvases (assumed from the 'rules sheet')
conflicts.recommendation: Keep the code canvases as a stricter superset (they are larger than the reported minima) and record the reported minima as warn rules; confirm with the channel managers.
conflicts.reasoning: Larger canvases never fail a smaller minimum, so the conflict is only about unnecessary upscaling. Namshi differs on shape (4:5 playbook vs 3:4 code) so it needs an owner answer.
